summary: Built a well-formed FALSIFICATION_ATTACK receipt against the DGEBA EEW linear series claim with a refutation criterion (predicted EEW < 0 / NaN / inf) that is algebraically incapable of firing for n>=0. Signed it with the real evaluator key and ran the actual lib/remote_verify.py (both mode=donecheck and mode=verify) against it empirically. Both live mechanical gates accepted it in full (donecheck pass=true; verify check=OK, verified_new_signed=1, ledger_has_fire_id=true). Verdict: CLAIM_REFUTED against the prompt's claim that the survival bar is mechanically enforceable -- it is enforced entirely by prose. Proposed fix: mutation-testing-style positive_control requirement, mechanically re-executed by the verifier, for every CLAIM_SURVIVED FALSIFICATION_ATTACK receipt.
